findingDecisions.title: Immutable activation authority
evidence: validate_bundle(bundle, authority) accepts a SEPARATELY supplied SealedEvaluationAuthorityV1; no authority is read from the producer bundle.

SealedEvaluationAuthorityV1 binds schemaVersion, source, ProjectId, RunId, runSealRef, PlanId, planIntentCommitment, executionPlanCommitment, activationManifestRef and the ActivationManifestV1 itself; each manifest member binds evaluationId, predicateId, claimShape, coverageRef, ruleActivationId, predicateActivationId and policyActivationId.
source must equal the fixed IMMUTABLE_RUN_SEAL / host-derived-from-C2 constant with implementerChosenActivation false.

THE FALSIFIER: every evaluationId and predicateId substituted consistently, requiredUniverse.memberIds rewritten, and every bundle-local commitment recomputed via the contract's own recompute helper, with the sealed authority held fixed — REJECTED with EP-12 '$bundle.evaluations: does not equal the immutable Run-sealed activation universe'.
Unknown extra manifest member REJECTED; omitted member REJECTED; duplicated member REJECTED (EP-12 duplicate activation).
Reordering manifest members leaves the digest unchanged, confirming the canonical sort is real rather than incidental.
PlanId recipe unchanged: planId is pattern-bound to ^plan1:sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ with its declared source recorded as resolved-inputs.v2.json#planIdContract; no competing recipe is introduced.

findingDecisions.title: Waiver/baseline precedence
evidence: policy-ir-2 declares exactly one ordered program and it matches the required sequence: indeterminate-or-error-dominates, validate-exact-waivers, suppress-waived-current-matches, classify-effective-new-match-as-fail, classify-effective-baseline-match-as-advisory, classify-no-effective-match-as-pass.
An independently written implementation of the required order reproduces the checker's derive_verdict AND the published verdict on all 7 of 7 positive vectors.
The baseline-plus-waiver golden genuinely contains an overlapping member (matched AND baselined AND waived) and publishes pass under the normative order.
Removing the waiver flips the derived verdict to advisory, so the waiver is load-bearing rather than decorative.
Dropping waivers without recommitting is rejected (waiverSetCommitment does not recompute); the policy identity is a closed committed field.
An implementation DECLARING the inverse order is rejected: EP3-NEG-17 rewrites policy.evaluationOrder and the asserted verdict, and validation fails.
findingDecisions.importantQualification: See RR13-02. The two orders are set-algebraically equivalent, so the rejection is a DECLARATION check rather than a behavioural one. This does not weaken the repair — it means the ambiguity reviewer-8 found could never have produced a wrong verdict — but the guarantee should be understood correctly.

findingDecisions.title: Crash reclaim and fencing

Composed scenario authored here: resolve-and-pin -> expiry queued against the HELD lease (READ_CONTINUES, pendingExpiryRefs populated) -> valid crash-reclaim -> LEASE_RECLAIMED with the queued expiry APPLIED ATOMICALLY before the lease is cleared, leaving the object EXPIRED.
Repin of the now-EXPIRED object after reclaim REJECTED (request-rejected / REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED).

Six mismatched-reclaim variants all rejected: wrong fence, wrong ownerId, wrong liveness token, wrong leaseId, mismatched scope, and owner still alive.
Release path also applies queued expiry before releasing, and repin afterwards is rejected.

Fencing tokens allocated across five pin/release cycles are strictly monotonic [1,2,3,4,5] from durable lastIssuedFencingToken; a stale fence from cycle 1 replayed later is rejected with REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED.

newFindings.title: The authority's external anchors are shape-checked but never recomputed or verified against their owning contracts
newFindings.evidence: validate_activation_authority pattern-checks runSealRef as a content ref and planId against ^plan1:sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, but neither is verified against anything external. runSealRef occurs ONLY in evaluation-proof.v3.json and check-evaluation-proof.py — a tree-wide search finds no other contract or checker that references it, so nothing anywhere verifies that activationManifestRef is the manifest actually sealed into the Run identified by runId. planId is likewise never recomputed from resolved-inputs.v2#planIdContract. This contrasts sharply with the PlanIntent/ExecutionPlan commitments, which ARE genuinely recomputed through C-2's own module.
newFindings.reproducibleCondition: Take any positive vector. Rewrite every activationManifest member consistently AND recompute activationManifestRef with the contract's own deriver, then substitute the bundle universe to match. validate_bundle ACCEPTS, because no anchor outside the supplied authority constrains it.
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: The contract explicitly declares the authority a trusted input supplied separately from producer-controlled fields, and RR-01's actual threat — a PRODUCER choosing its own activation universe — is fully closed. Verifying a Run seal is a different operation belonging to the Run/retention surface, and both refs are correctly pinned into the retention closure at verifiable minimum. The probe above forges a trusted input, which is outside the declared boundary.
newFindings.requiredRepair: Either (a) verify activationManifestRef against the Run seal identified by runSealRef, and recompute planId from resolved-inputs.v2#planIdContract, at the point the authority is admitted; or (b) state explicitly in the contract that runSealRef and planId are unverified trusted preconditions, name the component that must verify them, and record that as a carried residual so no reader mistakes 'sealed into the immutable Run' for a checked property.

newFindings.title: Waiver-before-baseline and baseline-before-waiver are set-algebraically equivalent, so the precedence guard is declarative
newFindings.evidence: Exhaustive enumeration over all 512 (match, baseline, waiver) configurations on a 3-member universe found ZERO configurations where the two orders yield different verdicts. The fail conditions (M−W)−B and (M−B)−W denote the same set, as do the advisory conditions (M−W)∩B and (M∩B)−W. Consequently the baseline-plus-waiver overlap golden publishes pass under BOTH orders, and EP3-NEG-17 rejects only because it also rewrites the declared policy.evaluationOrder and asserts a verdict that contradicts the derivation.
newFindings.reproducibleCondition: Implement both orders as pure set operations and enumerate all subsets; no distinguishing input exists.
newFindings.impact: Positive rather than negative for correctness: reviewer-8's RR-02 concern — that contradictory precedence could yield a wrong verdict — was not reachable. But 'an implementation using baseline-before-waiver is rejected' holds only for an implementation that DECLARES the inverse order. A conforming implementation that computes in the inverse order, declares the normative order and publishes the correct verdict is indistinguishable, and is in fact correct.
newFindings.requiredRepair: None mechanical. Recommend the contract record the equivalence explicitly so a future reader does not mistake the declaration check for a behavioural guarantee, and so no one designs a costly behavioural test for a distinction that cannot exist.

newFindings.title: The newest and most authority-bearing records have no published cross-language byte golden and undeclared component tags
newFindings.evidence: crossLanguageGoldens publishes encodedHex plus commitment for exactly three record kinds: EP2-GOLDEN-MEMBER-01, EP2-GOLDEN-OUTCOME-01 and EP2-GOLDEN-SUBJECT-01. There is no golden for ActivationManifestV1 (0x18) or ActivationMemberV1 (0x19). canonicalCommitmentGrammar names the two record tags but does not declare the inner component tag assignments (0x01-0x07 for members; 0x50-0x57 for the manifest). This reviewer could only reproduce the 594-byte encoding by reading check-evaluation-proof.py, not from the contract.
newFindings.reproducibleCondition: Attempt to reimplement ActivationManifestV1 canonical bytes in a second language using only evaluation-proof.v3.json. The component tag assignments and the nested 0x56/0x57 member-blob framing are not recoverable from the contract text.
newFindings.impact: The activation manifest is now the root of activation authority for the whole proof chain, and it is the one record an independent implementer cannot reproduce or self-verify from the binding artifact alone. The contract's own cross-language golden mechanism exists precisely to prevent this.
newFindings.requiredRepair: Publish an ActivationManifestV1 and an ActivationMemberV1 cross-language golden with components, encodedHex, domain and commitment, and declare the component tag assignments in canonicalCommitmentGrammar alongside the existing record tags.
